reasoning_content:
Very interesting! When I run tileserver-gl directly with the same config and the same data volume, it works — "Starting server... Startup complete" with no errors and no crash (it ran until my 15-second timeout). No "Not valid input file" error either.

So why does the compose container keep crashing with "Not valid input file"?

The difference: the compose container's command is:
```yaml
command:
  [
    "--config",
    "/data/config.json",
    "--public_url",
    "https://tiles.localhost",
  ]
```

Let me look at the compose file again:

```yaml
  tileserver:
    image: maptiler/tileserver-gl:v5.6.0
    container_name: qonnectra_tileserver_dev
    restart: unless-stopped
    user: "1000:1000"
    volumes:
      - ./tiles:/data:ro
    command:
      [
        "--config",
        "/data/config.json",
        "--public_url",
        "https://tiles.localhost",
      ]
    expose:
      - "8080"
```

Hmm — the image's default CMD is probably `["--config", "/data/config.json"]` with ENTRYPOINT being tileserver. The compose command replaces the CMD, but the entrypoint stays the same. When I ran it directly with `--config /data/config.json --public_url http://tiles.localhost`... wait, when I ran it directly, I specified the entrypoint as the image's default? I ran `docker run --rm -v ... --user 1000:1000 maptiler/tileserver-gl:v5.6.0 --config /data/config.json --public_url http://tiles.localhost` — the image's ENTRYPOINT is probably `["/usr/src/app/index.js"]` or similar, and my arguments were appended to it. Same as what compose does (command appends to the entrypoint).

The only difference between my successful run and the compose one: `--public_url http://tiles.localhost` vs. `https://tiles.localhost`. Hmm, would that cause a "Not valid input file" error? Unlikely...

Wait, actually — maybe the compose container is still using an old version of the file from before I created the placeholder... no, I created the placeholder at 17:35, and the container was restarted around 17:34:49 according to the inspect Started time... hmm, the inspect showed Started=17:34:49, which is before I created the file (17:35). Let me check the current state again — the restart loop may have already picked up the new file. The log tail showed 4 "Not valid" lines, but they may all have been from before 17:35.

No wait — the timeline: I created the mbtiles at 17:35:0x (ls shows 17:35). Then I ran `docker compose up -d tileserver`, and the log showed "Starting container" and the same "Not valid" messages. But `docker logs` shows the history since the container was created, including the old entries. The log entries shown may have all been from before the file existed.

Let me check the latest logs and the current container state.
